questions.q: What is the correct order of the Cosmos DB resource hierarchy?
options: Account, then database, then container
Container, then database, then account
Database, then account, then container
There is no hierarchy — all resources exist at the same level
questions.explain: Every Cosmos DB resource sits inside this strict three-level hierarchy: account at the top, then database, then container.

questions.q: What is chosen at the account level and generally can't be changed afterward without creating a new account?
options: The API type (Core, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, or Table)
The partition key path
The throughput in RU/s
The container name
questions.explain: The API is selected at account creation (e.g. --kind GlobalDocumentDB for Core API) and is fixed for that account's life.

questions.q: At which level is the partition key path set, and how permanent is that decision?
options: At the container level, and it's effectively permanent for the life of the container
At the account level, and it can be changed at any time
At the database level, and it has no real consequences
Partition keys are not set anywhere during provisioning
questions.explain: The container's --partition-key-path is mandatory at creation and, per this lesson, effectively permanent — the most consequential provisioning decision.

questions.q: What does a Cosmos DB database (the middle level of the hierarchy) represent?
options: A logical grouping of containers within an account, roughly analogous to a SQL Server database as a namespace
The physical machine storing the data
A single document's schema definition
An entirely separate Cosmos DB account
questions.explain: The database level is a logical namespace grouping containers, and can optionally have shared throughput across those containers.

questions.q: What does the --throughput flag set when creating a container?
options: The provisioned Request Units per second (RU/s) for that container
The maximum number of documents allowed in the container
The number of Azure regions the container replicates to
The API type used by that specific container
questions.explain: --throughput 400 requests 400 RU/s of provisioned throughput, the currency covered fully in Lesson 34.
